Theme

Work & responsibility

presentation noun

a talk given at work

also give a presentation, present

classical

Cic. Or. 212: expositiōnēs rērum (Lewis & Short)
Quint. 4.2.2

expositiō, expositiōnis f.

noun, third declension

a setting forth, a presentation

Lewis & Short: a setting forth, an exposition; in Cicero and Quintilian the part of a speech that lays out the facts. To give a presentation is rem expōnere.

Other words

  • dēmōnstrātiō, dēmōnstrātiōnis f. — a showing, pointing out

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 3.220 (Lewis & Short)

    Where the point is to show something, with the finger or on a screen.

Examples

  • Crās rem collēgīs expōnere dēbeō.

    I have to give a presentation to my colleagues tomorrow.composed

See also meeting, office.

SourcesLewis & Short: expositio · Lewis & Short: expono · Lewis & Short: demonstratio
